title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on the construction and operation of new data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. This measure aims to curb rapid AI infrastructure growth, protect environmental resources, and encourage more responsible, sustainable deployment of AI technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is designed to curb the ecological footprint of AI technologies. It requires firms to evaluate and reduce the energy use, carbon emissions, and waste produced by training and operating AI systems, and to report on their compliance with new environmental standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction or operation of new data centers that support AI workloads. This pause is intended to allow policymakers to assess and address concerns over environmental impact, energy consumption, and resource allocation before allowing such facilities to resume.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 requires AI developers to assess and mitigate the environmental footprint of their systems, including energy usage and resource consumption. It establishes reporting standards, carbon‑offset obligations, and encourages research into greener AI technologies.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a U.S. law proposal that seeks to strengthen the safety and security of artificial intelligence systems. It aims to set regulatory standards, establish oversight mechanisms, and enforce measures to protect public interests and ensure responsible AI development and deployment.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes rules and oversight for the use of artificial intelligence across different industry sectors, aiming to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It sets sector‑specific guidelines, regulatory frameworks, and enforcement mechanisms to manage AI risks while encouraging innovation.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent artificial‑intelligence companies from charging excessively high prices and manipulating wage levels, protecting consumers and workers. The legislation would establish regulatory oversight and enforcement tools to monitor and curb unfair pricing and wage‑setting practices in the AI market.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House urges Congress to refuse any extra funding or special regulatory help for companies or financial institutions that are in trouble because of stress in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, the policy calls for providing assistance to all Americans who have been harmed by these disruptions.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a proposed law that regulates the use of artificial intelligence technologies in veterinary medicine. It aims to ensure that AI tools used in animal care are safe, transparent, and ethically responsible, while also protecting animal welfare and patient data privacy.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits AI systems from acting as independent doctors, requiring that all medical diagnoses and prescriptions be performed or directly supervised by licensed human physicians. The law also mandates that any AI tools used in healthcare be transparent about their limitations, undergo rigorous safety testing, and remain subject to continuous human oversight to protect patient safety.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies to conduct thorough assessments of their AI systems, identifying and mitigating bias, safety risks, and discriminatory impacts. It also mandates transparency and accountability measures, ensuring that stakeholders can understand how algorithmic decisions are made and can hold developers responsible for adverse outcomes.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect elections from manipulation by AI-generated misinformation. It proposes legal measures and safeguards to detect and prevent deceptive AI content that could influence voters.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to set strict standards for developing and using AI so that the systems are safe, transparent, and accountable. It calls for government, industry, and academic collaboration to promote trustworthy AI technologies and protect the public’s interests.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law that requires companies that develop or deploy artificial intelligence systems in Virginia to fully disclose how those systems work, including the data they use and any known biases. It establishes a state commission to oversee compliance, review disclosures, and impose penalties on firms that fail to meet the transparency standards.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law designed to ensure that artificial intelligence tools used in Veterans Affairs claim processing are transparent, reliable, and fair. It establishes standards and oversight mechanisms so that VA staff and contractors can monitor AI decisions, address biases, and protect veterans’ rights throughout the claims process.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Act is designed to protect consumers from misleading or deceptive use of AI in products and services. It requires companies to clearly disclose when AI is used and to ensure that AI‑driven decisions are fair, accurate, and not deceptive.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act requires organizations that develop or deploy advanced AI to implement robust security controls, conduct regular risk assessments, and establish incident response plans to protect against malicious use of AI systems. It also creates a regulatory body to oversee compliance, set industry standards, and promote collaboration between governments, industry, and academia to enhance AI security readiness across the nation.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a new task force led by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems. Its goal is to identify and fix AI vulnerabilities, set industry standards, and protect critical infrastructure and national security from AI‑related risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential harms from AI systems, requiring organizations to adopt systematic risk management practices. It also sets standards for security, accountability, and oversight to protect public safety, data privacy, and the integrity of AI technologies.
